nodes.name: Anchoring atomic Mo on metal hydroxides
nodes.procedure: 20 mg of metal hydroxide nanosheets was suspended in 50 mL of absolute ethanol and sonicated for 15 min. Notably, ethanol was deeply dewatered by adding calcium hydride and distilling before use. Then, a certain amount of 2 mg mL⁻¹ MoCl₅ ethanol solution was quickly added into the above suspension under vigorous stirring. The mixture was stirred for 12 h to ensure the complete reaction of MoCl₅. Afterward, the solid phase was collected by vacuum filtration with nylon filter membrane (pore size 0.22 μm), washed with ethanol three times and dried at 40 °C for 12 h. The obtained Mo-based SACs are denoted as Mo-n%/M(OH)x (M = Mg, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu and Zn; n% represents the dosage mass ratio of Mo element to metal hydroxides, which is omitted when it is 1 %).

nodes.description: Aerobic oxidation of DBT model compound - comparison of all Mo SACs
nodes.source_text: For aerobic oxidation tests, dibenzothiophene (DBT)... was used as a model compound. Of all investigated SACs (Figures 3A and S10), Mo/Co(OH)₂ exhibits the best catalytic performance, achieving complete conversion of DBT within 3.5 h (an initial rate of 5.73×10^{-3} mol L^{-1} h^{-1}). Reaction conditions: 1 mg of catalyst, 30 mL of model oil, 110°C, 40 mL/min of airflow rate.

nodes.description: Low temperature AODS of DBT at 60°C with Mo-3%/Co(OH)₂
nodes.source_text: Mo-3%/Co(OH)₂ showed good activity even at 60°C due to the excellent O₂ activation performance (Figure S15). The TOF values were calculated and found to be several hundred times higher than that of conventional MMOs (Table S5).
As for the hydrogenation diesel, almost all the sulfides were fully converted in 50 min... The oxidized diesel was then extracted using methanol, yielding a sulfur content of 3.3±0.2 ppm (Table S8).

nodes.source_text: As for the straight-run diesel, most of the sulfides have been converted in 3h except for a small amount of BT's derivatives, and a sulfur content of 16.6±0.9 ppm was obtained after the subsequent solvent extraction.

To test the generality of our catalyst, we adopted three other typical sulfides, namely, benzothiophene (BT), 3-methylbenzothiophene (3-MBT), and 4,6-dimethyl-dibenzothiophene (4,6-DMDBT) for AODS experiments. The reactivities of all four sulfides used follow the order of BT < 3-MBT < 4,6-DMDBT < DBT (Figures S16 and S17).
Sole Co(OH)₂ does not show any catalytic activity, proving that the atomic Mo site is the only active center (Figure S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co(OH)2 nanosheet has a width of around 400 nm and thickness of 0.8–1 nm, with no apparent change after Mo anchoring.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co(OH)2 nanosheet is in a width of around 400 nm and a thickness of around 0.8–1 nm (Figures 1B and 1C).

nodes.characterization_summary: No apparent change in morphology observed after anchoring of atomic Mo sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the anchoring of atomic Mo sites, no apparent change in morphology was observed (Figures 1D and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Formation of atomic Mo sites on Co(OH)2 surface confirmed; STEM elemental mapping shows uniform Mo dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We prove the formation of atomic Mo sites on the surface of Co(OH)2 with high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) (Figures 1E, 1F, and S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Actual Mo composition determined via ICP-AES (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The actual composition was finally determined via inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge EXAFS shows strong FT peak at 1.8 Å for Mo-O coordination; absence of Mo-Mo (2.8 Å) and Mo-O-Mo (3.6 Å) confirms atomic Mo state; CN=4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) of Mo K-edge was used to investigate the coordination environment... strong Fourier transformed (FT) peak located around 1.8 Å, attributed to the scattering of Mo-O coordination.

properties.description: Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure spectrum for MoO2

nodes.characterization_summary: WT contour plots display only one maximum intensity corresponding to Mo-O coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The WT contour plots of Mo/Co(OH)2 display only one maximum intensity, corresponding to the Mo-O coordination (Figure 2B).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge XANES shows valence between Mo(VI) and Mo(V) for SACs; correlation with second peak position; lowest oxidation state of 5.11 for Mo on Co(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Correlation between the oxidation state of Mo and the position of the second peak in XANES spectra (Figures 2D and 2E) reveals that the valence of Mo sites in SACs is between Mo(VI) and Mo(V)... Detailed valence states of Mo are summarized in Table S3, which shows a lowest oxidation state of 5.11 for single-atom Mo on Co(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Mo 3d XPS confirms valence between Mo(VI) and Mo(V) for SACs; lowest oxidation state of 5.11 for Mo on Co(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in agreement with the result from high-resolution XPS Mo 3d spectra (Figures 2F and S9). Detailed valence states of Mo are summarized in Table S3, which shows a lowest oxidation state of 5.11 for single-atom Mo on Co(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: No change in powder XRD pattern after Mo anchoring, indicating absence of substrate reconstruction and nanoparticulate Mo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Expectedly, no change was observed in the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Co(OH)2 and Mo/Co(OH)2 (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Identical band gap for Co(OH)2 and Mo/Co(OH)2, indicating negligible impact from SACs on support electronic structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectra of Co(OH)2 and Mo/Co(OH)2 show identical band gap (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform dispersion of Mo element on Co(OH)2 host nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM elemental mapping (Figure 1G) demonstrates the uniform dispersion of Mo element on the host nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Absence of chlorine confirms complete dissociation of Mo-Cl bond and formation of Mo-O bond.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the absence of chlorine (Cl) in the obtained Mo/Co(OH)2 (Figure S6) suggests the complete dissociation of Mo–Cl bond and subsequent formation of Mo–O bond.
